en: The Therāpadāna, Upāli-vagga 1: The Apadāna of the Elder Upāli, Nephew I was a monk in the dispensation of Kassapa, the Great Sage. At that time, I was a nephew; I was called Upāli. Having heard the Dhamma from the Teacher, I took refuge in the Triple Gem. I went forth into homelessness under the dispensation of the Buddha. For twenty thousand years I practiced the holy life; I observed the precepts with constant mindfulness. When my life had reached its end, I passed away from that world. I was reborn in the realm of the Thirty-three gods. From there, passing through various celestial abodes, I attained the state of a Wheel-turning Monarch. In that existence, I ruled over the four continents; I governed the earth for eighty-four thousand years. Then, having passed away from that human state, I was reborn in the realm of the Tusita gods. There too, I enjoyed divine pleasures for a long time; I dwelt in bliss for eighty-four thousand aeons.

From there, passing through various celestial abodes, I attained the status of a Universal Monarch. In that existence, I ruled over the four continents; I governed the earth for eighty-four thousand years. Then, having passed away from that human state, I was reborn in the realm of the Yāma gods. Surrounded by a thousand whose taints were destroyed, the Leader of the World remained devoted to seclusion.
I went to dwell in seclusion.
Clothed in an antelope skin,
carrying a triple staff;
I saw the Leader of the World, surrounded by the community of bhikkhus;
having placed my deerskin robe over one shoulder, [I approached him].
Having placed my hands in añjali and paid homage to the Perfectly Awakened One,
I praised the Leader of the World.
Just as those born from eggs, those born from moisture, those born spontaneously, and those born from a womb—
such as all the birds beginning with crows—
Always moving through the sky:
"Whatever beings there are,
whether possessing consciousness or lacking consciousness;"
All those [scents] are contained within your knowledge, submerged therein—
both the fragrances found upon the mountains and those that grow elsewhere.
Even all those [trees] on the highest peak of the Himalayas do not equal even a fraction of your virtue.
This world, together with its devas, was plunged into the darkness of delusion;
now that your wisdom shines forth, it is illuminated.
The darkness has been dispelled.
Just as when the sun has set,
beings become shrouded in gloom.
Thus, when a Buddha has not appeared,
the world is shrouded in darkness,
just as when the sun has not yet risen.
He always dispels darkness;
even so, O Best of Buddhas,
you always destroy darkness.
You are one who has exerted yourself in striving,
O Buddha, in this world with its devas;
by your delight in kamma—
He smiled at the vast multitude.
Having rejoiced in all of that,
the Great Sage Padumuttara—
The wise one rose up into the sky like a king of swans in the air;
having risen up, the Fully Awakened One—
The Great Seer Padumuttara,
the Teacher standing in the sky,
spoke these verses.
This knowledge that has been established,
joined with similes,
I shall now proclaim.
Listen to me as I speak:
"Eighteen times he shall become a king of the gods."
He will dwell upon the earth, ruling over three hundred kingdoms;
and twenty-five times more, he will rule the world.
He will become a wheel-turning monarch;
his local sovereignty will be vast and beyond counting.
In a hundred thousand aeons,
one born of the Okkāka clan,
known by the name Gotama by lineage, will appear.
The Teacher shall appear in the world. For,
having passed away from the Tusita heaven,
impelled by the root of his white merit;
Born into a lowly caste,
he will be named Upāli;
later, having gone forth into homelessness, he will—
Having shunned evil,
and having fully understood all taints,
he will attain Nibbāna, free from taints.
And the Buddha Gotama,
the son of the Sakyas of great renown,
was pleased with his mastery of the Vinaya.
He will place me at the very head of these:
"I have gone forth out of faith;
my task is done, and I am free from taints."
Having fully understood all taints,
I dwell free from taints;
and the Blessed One is compassionate toward me.
I have disciplined myself with confidence;
delighted by my own deeds,
I dwell free from taints.
Restrained by the Pātimokkha and the five sense faculties,
I uphold the entire Vinaya.
A mine of jewels alone.
And recognizing my virtues,
the Teacher, unsurpassed in the world, [spoke thus].
Having sat in the community of bhikkhus,
he placed me in the foremost position.
The four analytical knowledges—
And these eight liberations have been realized; the six direct knowledges have been attained;
the Buddha’s teaching has been accomplished.”
Thus indeed the venerable elder Upāli spoke these verses.
This is the first legend of the elder Upāli, the nephew.
